newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia may delay subway construction - paper.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia may delay subway construction - paper.

text.p: Construction of a $2.2 billion underground rail system in Indonesia's capital of Jakarta, scheduled to start in June, may be delayed because of financial problems, Kompas newspaper reported on Monday.
"We all want to see the construction of the subway start faster, but how can we do it if we don't have the resources," the newspaper quoted Jakarta governor Surjadi Soedirdja as saying.

The official Antara news agency reported earlier this month that businessman Aburizal Bakrie, who heads a consortium of Indonesian, Japanese and European companies, said the construction would begin in June.

Kompas said the government wanted to keep subway ticket prices as low as possible, but investors seemed to have their own calculation and were worried about return on their investment if fares were too low.
The paper gave no further details.
Soedirdja said funding was the main problem in the construction of the 14.5-km (nine mile) undergound line which will link two business districts.
"The only problem is funding. We don't face any problem in other subjects. We already have the design and we don't have problems in the technology," he said.

The subway which links Blok M in south Jakarta and the historic Kota area in the north has been expected to be completed by August 17, 2001, to coincide with the country's 56th anniversary of independence.
Bustling Jakarta is home to nearly 10 million people and already faces chronic traffic jams, especially in the morning and afternoon peak hours.

The Jakarta Post newspaper has said the city administration had initially planned to raise $25 million per year for five years as its equity in the project and another $35 million for 25 years to pay back loans.
